sources.M42: Montgomery, Alamein operations despatch, London Gazette 38196: on 14 September 1942, 44th Division relieved the New Zealanders and 10th Armoured Division entered X Corps' rear training concentration; X Corps was the armoured exploitation command. Game strengths and exact map entries are estimates. https://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/UN/UK/LondonGazette/38196.pdf

name: Alamein offensive preparation: 7 September–22 October 1942 (linked research)

aim.cw: Hold the Alamein line, assemble enough strength and supply for a deliberate offensive, then choose when and where to strike.
aim.axis: Keep the Alamein front intact, protect fuel and prepare reserves against a Commonwealth breakthrough.

about: Linked two-day preparation up to the eve of the historical 23 October offensive. The Commonwealth attack date does not prevent an earlier or different attack. The 44th Division, X Corps and 10th Armoured Division enter as aggregate counters on a model date aligned to their documented 14 September reorganisation; their strengths and entry points are estimates. The current rules allow digging and stockpiling but do not model the full mine belt, artillery ammunition plan, training or deception programme.

add_units.name: 44th British Division group
add_units.arrives_note: 44th Division relieved the New Zealand Division in the line around 14 September. This aggregate counter's 7,000 men and exact map entry are estimates.

add_units.name: X Corps HQ
add_units.arrives_note: X Corps trained and re-equipped roughly 50 miles behind the Alamein line. The 14 September game entry at Alexandria is a map proxy, not its documented headquarters location.

add_units.name: 10th Armoured Division group
add_units.arrives_note: 10th Armoured Division joined X Corps' rear training concentration on 14 September. This aggregate counter's 180 serviceable tanks and Alexandria entry are estimates.
